sentences.text:
Appearance:
 Shri Sanjay Kumar Sharma - Advocate for the petitioner.
Shri Hemant Sharma-Govt. Adv. appearing on behalf of Ad  General.

Ms. Aayukta Sharma-Advocate for the respondents no. 2 &
 ORDER 1] Heard finally with the consent of the parties.

2] This petition has been filed by the petitioners under Section 482 of Cr.P.C./Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for quashment of FIR bearing Crime No.296/2023 for the offence punishable under Sections 363,
366(A), 376(2)(n), 376 of IPC and 3/4, 5(L)/6 of the POCSO, registered at Police Station Dharampuri, District Dhar, and other consequential proceedings arising out of the said crime number.
3] Counsel for the petitioner, at the outset, has submitted that the parties have settled their disputes out of the Court.
It is also submitted that the prosecutrix has already been examined in the trial court and has not supported the prosecution and has turned hostile.
It is also submitted that the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8558 2 MCRC-14527-2026 prosecutrix got married to the applicant and out of the wedlock they have a daughter.

It is further submitted that the affidavits regarding the compromise have also been filed on record, including the application for no objection,
and in such circumstances, the petition may be allowed.
4] Counsel for the private respondents has submitted that she has no objection if the present petition is allowed and the FIR is quashed.

1 5] Counsel for the State has submitted that appropriate order may be passed.
6] Having considered the rival submissions, perusal of the documents filed on record, as also the affidavits filed by the parties regarding the compromise, this Court is inclined to allow the present petition.

sentences.text: 7] Accordingly, the petition is hereby allowed and the FIR bearing Crime No.296/2023 for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366(A), 376(2)(n), 376 of IPC and 3/4, 5(L)/6 of the POCSO, registered at Police Station Dharampuri, District Dhar, and other consequential proceedings arising out of the said crime number
, so far as it relates to the present petitioner, are hereby quashed.
8] The M.Cr.C. stands allowed and all the interlocutory applications are also disposed of.
(SUBODH ABHYANKAR) JUDGE moni Jairam Bhatiya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27819599/
